PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Performing actions (such as generating rulesets) on WODM Decision Center or Rule Team Server can be slow and consume a lot of memory, sometimes leading to OutOfMemoryExceptions. How can the memory used be reduced and performance improved? 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

This document addresses memory issues when working with WebSphere Operational Decision Management Decision Center or Rule Team Server (RTS). For detailed recommendations on improving overall performance, refer to the document Improve Performance of Decision Center and RTS [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21584855]. For the purposes of this document, we will use RTS to refer to both entities, unless explicitly stated otherwise. 

Make sure you provide adequate heap size to RTS. It is normal to set a maximum heap size of 1024MB (using the JVM argument -Xmx). For large projects this value can be higher. Also make sure you have set the initial heap size to a reasonable amount (such as 512MB), using the JVM argument -Xms. 

 

In addition, please use the following recommendations to reduce memory consumption: 

 * Disable the flag to check the ruleset archive. In the RTS console, uncheck Project > Edit project options > Check the ruleset archive. By default, the ruleset archive is checked for syntax errors. You should turn this off only in testing environments to improve performance. If deploying to a production environment it is recommended that the ruleset check is activated. 
 * Disable Rule analysis checks. In the RTS console, uncheck Project > Edit Project options > Enable rule analysis. 
 * Accelerate ruleset generation by turning on Automatic Build. In the RTS console, check Project > Edit Project options > Build automatically. This will enable RTS to generate the IRL as soon as a rule is saved. If this is turned off, the first time a ruleset is generated, RTS will generate the IRL of the entire ruleset, which can be a performance bottleneck. 
 * If working with JRules 7.1 or earlier, configure RTS to store temporary data to a file rather than in memory by setting the custom parameter teamserver.build.archive.storage to the value file. The default value of this parameter is memory. If the value is set to file, the rule artifacts built when a ruleset is generated are stored in a cache in the file system of the application server machine. In RTS 6.x, navigate to the Admin tab in the RTS console to add the custom parameter. In RTS 7.x, in the RTS console, navigate to Config > Install Manager > Step 5: Set Configuration Parameters to add the custom parameter. Note that while this will reduce the memory used, the performance could deteriorate since data is written to and read from the file system. 
 * In ODM (v7.5 and later), the IRL cache is always file based, and its location is set by one of the Decision Center configuration parameters, defined in jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear/teamserver.war/WEB-INF/lib/teamserver-model-XXX.jar/ilog/rules/teamserver/preferences.properties:
   
   # Path where the files generated during the build should be.
   # The path is determined in the following order
   # - use of the following property
   # - use of the system property denoted by 'java.io.tmpdir' plus 'rtscache_<username>' (Ex: <temp dir>/rtscache_<username>)
   # - <server home>/rtscache_<username>
   # where username is given by the system property denoted by 'user.name'
   build.path = 
   
   By default, it will be the temp directory of your OS.


 * If you have a large project, we recommend you break the project down into multiple projects which are dependent on one another. This will reduce the size of the project currently being edited via the RTS console, and hence reduce the amount of resources required. 
 * If you see performance problems during synchronization between Rule Studio and RTS, please refer to the guidelines in Improve Performance of Synchronization between Rule Studio and Rule Team Server [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425548] .

QUESTION
 How do I migrate a rule project to JRules v7.0 and v7.1? 

ANSWER
This document focuses on migration to JRules v7.0 and v7.1. For migration to WebSphere Operational Decision Management v7.5, refer to Migrating from JRules to WODM [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589725]. 
Before proceeding with migration, determine how you use Rule Studio and possibly Rule Team Server (RTS) for managing your rules. If your use case falls under Scenarios 1 or 2 as described in Migrating to JRules v7.1 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21592060] (Rule Studio is the source of truth for your rules), then continue to follow the recommendations in this document. 

JRules v7.0 and v7.1 incorporated certain design changes that require special consideration when migrating. Start by reading the 7.1 documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global70.html] on migration. Incorporate the following recommendations if applicable to your environment: 

 * Avoid OutOfMemoryErrors [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21504807] in Rule Studio during migration. 
 * Update decision tables and ruleflows to the v7.x format. Open the v6.x rule project in Rule Studio v7, modify each decision table and ruleflow (by introducing fake changes) and then save it. 
 * Alternatively, use this Rule Studio plugin [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21459145] to programmatically migrate all decision tables and ruleflows from v6.7 to v7.x format, and remove all checks from decision tables for a faster build time. 
 * Check the migration of ruleflows [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global80.html], decision tables [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global83.html] and ruleset properties [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global86.html]. 
 * Ensure the priority property [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21448570] is migrated properly. 
 * Resolve problems if migrating decision tables from v5.x [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21514593]. 


Once the migration has been completed,  * Fix any ambiguities that may be reported for individual rules due to the changes to BAL constructs [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global94.html] introduced in v7.0. 
 * Resolve any compilation errors on the rules. 
 * Verify that the rulesets are generated correctly. 
 * Publish the migrated project to RTS, if your use case is classified as Scenario 2. You can discard the previous RTS version's schema, instead of also performing RTS database migration, since the assumption is that only the latest artifacts from the Rule Studio project need to be maintained in RTS.

QUESTION
 How can I improve the performance of Operational Decision Management (ODM) Decision Center and WebSphere ILOG Rule Team Server (RTS)? 

ANSWER
 

This document addresses how to improve the performance when working with ODM Decision Center or Rule Team Server (RTS) . For the purposes of this document, we will use RTS to refer to both entities, unless explicitly stated otherwise.

You can incorporate the following recommendations, if applicable to your environment: 

Installation  * Separate your installations of Rule Execution Server (RES) and RTS. A high RES execution load will negatively impact RTS performance. Check if you been seeing heavier than normal RES execution loads during the period of poor RTS performance. 
 * If possible, migrate to v7.1.1.4 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21591798] or later [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589725], since certain performance improvements, especially for ruleset extraction and editing, have been incorporated. This would require all the other components (such as RES, Rule Studio, Decision Server, Rule Designer, Decision Validation Services) to be migrated to the same version. (If you face compile errors in RTS after migrating, refer to this technote [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21586358].) 
 * Dedicate enough processing resources (CPUs) to RTS. Deploy RTS to a cluster [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21400812] on your application server, to improve performance and scalability. 
 * Make sure you provide adequate heap size to RTS. It is normal to set a maximum heap size of 1024MB (using the JVM argument -Xmx). For large projects this value can be higher. Also make sure you have set the initial heap size to a reasonable amount (such as 512MB), using the JVM argument -Xms. 
 * Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated to RTS. 
 * Make sure that the link between the application server and the database has low latency (check ping round trip times between servers), sufficient bandwidth, and that the datasource is set up for effective connection pooling. See Decision Center performance and Tomcat datasource [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21623876] for an illustration of how the datasource configuration can negatively affect performance.


Startup and Indexing  * In ODM, by default the Business Console Solr Indexing happens at every start of the application server. The JVM hosting the Business Console may require an increase in maximum heap memory depending on the number of rule artifacts to be indexed per baseline. It is possible to avoid indexing to happen at every start of the application server by specifying a search.SolrEmbeddedDataDir value as per the documentation:http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/topic/com.ibm.odm.distrib.config.was/shared_config_topics/con_dcbc_solr_parameters.html [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/topic/com.ibm.odm.distrib.config.was/shared_config_topics/con_dcbc_solr_parameters.html]



Logging In  * Reduce the delay when logging into RTS [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21450448] for the first time after the application server has been restarted.


Browsing  * If using v7.1.x or later, improve the responsiveness while browsing artifacts [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21585248]. 
 * When browsing rules in v7.1.1.0 and prior, eliminate long pauses [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21439425] that may occur after a period of inactivity.


Editing  * If you have a large project, we recommend you break the project down into multiple projects which are dependent on one another. This will reduce the size of the project currently being edited, and hence reduce the amount of resources required. 
 * Reduce the size of the Business Object Model (BOM) by removing members, classes and verbalizations that are not used. You can also split the BOM into multiple smaller BOMs, and use categories. 
 * Reduce the size of large Decision Tables by splitting them into multiple smaller tables. There is no hard set limit and only experience with a specific application and setup can show what is a practical maximum, but it is typically recommended to have no more than a few hundred rows per Decision Table (i.e 300-400). 
 * Turn off Symmetry, Overlap and Gap checking for Decision Tables. Navigate to the decision table and edit it. In the view "Step 2: Table", click on the icon with a magnifying glass above the decision table, with the tooltip "Edit table properties". In the Table Properties editor, uncheck the Symmetry, Overlap and Gap checks. Note that these checks will no longer be enforced while editing decision tables. 
 * Edit Decision Tables using the Edit all table [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.bu.rules%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DCBU_DCenter_Rules2524.html] mode, In this mode there is no round trip to the server to validate input (as is normally the case with the default Decision Table editor) until the changes are committed using the submit button. 
 * Disable Rule analysis checks by unchecking Project > Edit Project options > Enable rule analysis.


Synchronization  * Improve the performance during synchronization [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425548] with Rule Studio or Rule Designer. 
 * Improve the performance of publishing and updating RuleDocs [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21623688].


Managing Baselines  * Improve the response time of Manage Baselines [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501448].


Ruleset Extraction  * Improve the time taken to extract rulesets [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21590218] and generate RuleApp archives.


Decision Validation Services (DVS) tests  * Improve the response time of DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21588859] conducted from RTS.


Database Maintenance  * The RTS database can become burdened with old records. Archive the RTS database (v7.1 and earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global1623.html], and ODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.customizing%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Customizing3220.html]), to avoid performance problems.


In addition, refer to the following documents:  * Improving Rule Team Server performance [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global205.html]. 
 * Improving the performance of Decision Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]. 
 * Enhancing the performance of Rule Team Server in the redpaper Proven Practices for Enhancing Performance: A Q&A for IBM WebSphere ILOG BRMS 7.1 [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redpapers/pdfs/redp4775.pdf]. 
 * Memory and Performance issues while using Rule Team Server [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430582]


If the above recommendations do not help, contact IBM support with the following information:  * Environment details including the application server, JDK, database and operating system. 
 * RTS server logs, including FFDC logs if working with WebSphere Application Server. 
 * The typical behavior of RTS users: Are they mostly viewing or editing? Is there a lot of ruleset generation going on simultaneously while editing? 
 * The typical load on RTS, including the number of simultaneous users and number of rulesets being generated 

RELATED INFORMATION

Improve Performance of Rule Studio and Rule Designer [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589514]

Performing actions (such as generating rulesets) on WODM Decision Center or Rule Team Server can be slow and consume a lot of memory, sometimes leading to OutOfMemoryExceptions.
How can the memory used be reduced and performance improved?
This document addresses memory issues when working with WebSphere Operational Decision Management Decision Center or Rule Team Server (RTS).
For detailed recommendations on improving overall performance, refer to the document Improve Performance of Decision Center and RTS [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21584855].
For the purposes of this document, we will use RTS to refer to both entities, unless explicitly stated otherwise.
Make sure you provide adequate heap size to RTS.
It is normal to set a maximum heap size of 1024MB (using the JVM argument -Xmx).
For large projects this value can be higher.
Also make sure you have set the initial heap size to a reasonable amount (such as 512MB), using the JVM argument -Xms.
In addition, please use the following recommendations to reduce memory consumption:
* Disable the flag to check the ruleset archive.
In the RTS console, uncheck Project > Edit project options > Check the ruleset archive.
By default, the ruleset archive is checked for syntax errors.
You should turn this off only in testing environments to improve performance.
If deploying to a production environment it is recommended that the ruleset check is activated.
In the RTS console, uncheck Project > Edit Project options > Enable rule analysis.
* Accelerate ruleset generation by turning on Automatic Build.
In the RTS console, check Project > Edit Project options > Build automatically.
This will enable RTS to generate the IRL as soon as a rule is saved.
If this is turned off, the first time a ruleset is generated, RTS will generate the IRL of the entire ruleset, which can be a performance bottleneck.
* If working with JRules 7.1 or earlier, configure RTS to store temporary data to a file rather than in memory by setting the custom parameter teamserver.build.archive.storage to the value file.
The default value of this parameter is memory.
If the value is set to file, the rule artifacts built when a ruleset is generated are stored in a cache in the file system of the application server machine.
In RTS 6.x, navigate to the Admin tab in the RTS console to add the custom parameter.
In RTS 7.x, in the RTS console, navigate to Config > Install Manager > Step 5: Set Configuration Parameters to add the custom parameter.
Note that while this will reduce the memory used, the performance could deteriorate since data is written to and read from the file system.

* In ODM (v7.5 and later), the IRL cache is always file based, and its location is set by one of the Decision Center configuration parameters, defined in jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear/teamserver.war/WEB-INF/lib/teamserver-model-XXX.jar/ilog/rules/teamserver/preferences.properties:
# Path where the files generated during the build should be.
# The path is determined in the following order
# - use of the system property denoted by 'java.io.tmpdir' plus 'rtscache_<username>' (Ex: <temp dir>/rtscache_<username>)
# where username is given by the system property denoted by 'user.name'
By default, it will be the temp directory of your OS.

This document focuses on migration to JRules v7.0 and v7.1.
For migration to WebSphere Operational Decision Management v7.5, refer to Migrating from JRules to WODM [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589725].
Before proceeding with migration, determine how you use Rule Studio and possibly Rule Team Server (RTS) for managing your rules.

If your use case falls under Scenarios 1 or 2 as described in Migrating to JRules v7.1 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21592060] (Rule Studio is the source of truth for your rules), then continue to follow the recommendations in this document.
JRules v7.0 and v7.1 incorporated certain design changes that require special consideration when migrating.

Start by reading the 7.1 documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global70.html] on migration.
Incorporate the following recommendations if applicable to your environment:
* Avoid OutOfMemoryErrors [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21504807] in Rule Studio during migration.
* Update decision tables and ruleflows to the v7.x format.
Open the v6.x rule project in Rule Studio v7, modify each decision table and ruleflow (by introducing fake changes) and then save it.

* Alternatively, use this Rule Studio plugin [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21459145] to programmatically migrate all decision tables and ruleflows from v6.7 to v7.x format, and remove all checks from decision tables for a faster build time.

* Check the migration of ruleflows [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global80.html], decision tables [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global83.html] and ruleset properties [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global86.html].
* Ensure the priority property [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21448570] is migrated properly.

performance; RTS; JRules; Rule Team Server; WODM; improvement; Decision Center TECHNOTE (FAQ) QUESTION
How can I improve the performance of Operational Decision Management (ODM) Decision Center and WebSphere ILOG Rule Team Server (RTS)? ANSWER
This document addresses how to improve the performance when working with ODM Decision Center or Rule Team Server (RTS) .
For the purposes of this document, we will use RTS to refer to both entities, unless explicitly stated otherwise.
You can incorporate the following recommendations, if applicable to your environment:
Installation  * Separate your installations of Rule Execution Server (RES) and RTS.
A high RES execution load will negatively impact RTS performance.
Check if you been seeing heavier than normal RES execution loads during the period of poor RTS performance.

* If possible, migrate to v7.1.1.4 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21591798] or later [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589725], since certain performance improvements, especially for ruleset extraction and editing, have been incorporated.
This would require all the other components (such as RES, Rule Studio, Decision Server, Rule Designer, Decision Validation Services) to be migrated to the same version.
(If you face compile errors in RTS after migrating, refer to this technote [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21586358].)
* Dedicate enough processing resources (CPUs) to RTS.
Deploy RTS to a cluster [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21400812] on your application server, to improve performance and scalability.
* Make sure you provide adequate heap size to RTS.
It is normal to set a maximum heap size of 1024MB (using the JVM argument -Xmx).
For large projects this value can be higher.
Also make sure you have set the initial heap size to a reasonable amount (such as 512MB), using the JVM argument -Xms.
* Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated to RTS.

* Make sure that the link between the application server and the database has low latency (check ping round trip times between servers), sufficient bandwidth, and that the datasource is set up for effective connection pooling.

See Decision Center performance and Tomcat datasource [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21623876] for an illustration of how the datasource configuration can negatively affect performance.
Startup and Indexing  * In ODM, by default the Business Console Solr Indexing happens at every start of the application server.
The JVM hosting the Business Console may require an increase in maximum heap memory depending on the number of rule artifacts to be indexed per baseline.

It is possible to avoid indexing to happen at every start of the application server by specifying a search.SolrEmbeddedDataDir value as per the documentation:http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/topic/com.ibm.odm.distrib.config.was/shared_config_topics/con_dcbc_solr_parameters.html [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/topic/com.ibm.odm.distrib.config.was/shared_config_topics/con_dcbc_solr_parameters.html]
Logging In  * Reduce the delay when logging into RTS [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21450448] for the first time after the application server has been restarted.
Browsing  * If using v7.1.x or later, improve the responsiveness while browsing artifacts [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21585248].
* When browsing rules in v7.1.1.0 and prior, eliminate long pauses [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21439425] that may occur after a period of inactivity.
Editing  * If you have a large project, we recommend you break the project down into multiple projects which are dependent on one another.
This will reduce the size of the project currently being edited, and hence reduce the amount of resources required.
* Reduce the size of the Business Object Model (BOM) by removing members, classes and verbalizations that are not used.
You can also split the BOM into multiple smaller BOMs, and use categories.
* Reduce the size of large Decision Tables by splitting them into multiple smaller tables.

There is no hard set limit and only experience with a specific application and setup can show what is a practical maximum, but it is typically recommended to have no more than a few hundred rows per Decision Table (i.e 300-400).
* Turn off Symmetry, Overlap and Gap checking for Decision Tables.
Navigate to the decision table and edit it.
In the view "Step 2: Table", click on the icon with a magnifying glass above the decision table, with the tooltip "Edit table properties".
In the Table Properties editor, uncheck the Symmetry, Overlap and Gap checks.
Note that these checks will no longer be enforced while editing decision tables.

* Edit Decision Tables using the Edit all table [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.bu.rules%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DCBU_DCenter_Rules2524.html] mode, In this mode there is no round trip to the server to validate input (as is normally the case with the default Decision Table editor) until the changes are committed using the submit button.
* Disable Rule analysis checks by unchecking Project > Edit Project options > Enable rule analysis.
Synchronization  * Improve the performance during synchronization [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425548] with Rule Studio or Rule Designer.
* Improve the performance of publishing and updating RuleDocs [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21623688].
Managing Baselines  * Improve the response time of Manage Baselines [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501448].
Ruleset Extraction  * Improve the time taken to extract rulesets [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21590218] and generate RuleApp archives.
Decision Validation Services (DVS) tests  * Improve the response time of DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21588859] conducted from RTS.
Database Maintenance  * The RTS database can become burdened with old records.

Archive the RTS database (v7.1 and earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global1623.html], and ODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.customizing%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Customizing3220.html]), to avoid performance problems.

In addition, refer to the following documents:  * Improving Rule Team Server performance [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global205.html].

* Improving the performance of Decision Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html].

* Enhancing the performance of Rule Team Server in the redpaper Proven Practices for Enhancing Performance: A Q&A for IBM WebSphere ILOG BRMS 7.1 [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redpapers/pdfs/redp4775.pdf].
* Memory and Performance issues while using Rule Team Server [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430582]
If the above recommendations do not help, contact IBM support with the following information:  * Environment details including the application server, JDK, database and operating system.
* RTS server logs, including FFDC logs if working with WebSphere Application Server.
* The typical behavior of RTS users: Are they mostly viewing or editing?
Is there a lot of ruleset generation going on simultaneously while editing?
* The typical load on RTS, including the number of simultaneous users and number of rulesets being generated RELATED INFORMATION
Improve Performance of Rule Studio and Rule Designer [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589514]

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)

CAUSE

ANSWER
Overview 

The v7.0 and later releases of the Rational products listed below use a common activation scheme. This technote outlines the activation product for the various products to help you get up and running as quickly as possible. 

You can now convert a trial (or evaluation) copy of the software to the production version of the same product without having to uninstall and reinstall the product. Additionally, if you own floating licenses of the products listed below you can now control usage of the products within your enterprise by using FLEXlm-based license keys as an optional feature (not available for Rational Data Architect and Method Composer).




"Activation Kit" or FLEXlm floating license keys required by these Rational products:

 * Rational Method Composer (as of v7.5.1)

 * Rational Software Architect (RSA) 
 * Rational Systems Developer (RSD) 
 * Rational Software Modeler (RSM) 
 * Rational Tester for SOA Quality 
 * Rational Developer for System I 
 * Rational Developer for System Z


** Rational Data Architect support Activation Kits only. FLEXlm license keys are not offered with these products. 

Activate your product after purchase! The 7.0 and later versions of the products listed above will expire 30 days after installation. Rational Application Developer will expire 60 days after installation. You will need to activate your product in order to use it after the expiration date. 

Activation if you own Authorized User licenses 

If you purchased an Authorized User license of the products listed above, you simply need to obtain and install an "activation kit" for your product that will convert it to a non-expiring version. Activation kits are product specific (they are not host-specific like Rational license keys). This means if you own multiple licenses of one of the products, you only need one activation kit and you can use it on any machine where the product is installed. For example, if you purchased two copies of IBM Rational Software Architect, you only need to obtain one activation kit and you can install it on both machines running Rational Software Architect. 

If you ordered media for your 7.0 or later product, you will find the activation kit on a CD in your software shipment. If you do not have a CD, you can obtain your activation kit by downloading it from your license account on the IBM Rational License Key Center website [http://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/]. The kit will show up in your license account that offers the v7.0 product license. Each of the products listed above will have a unique activation kit with the naming convention of "Product Name Multi platform Multilingual Activation Kit", e.g. "IBM Rational Software Architect v7.0 Multi platform Multilingual Activation Kit". Once you obtain the activation kit, run the activation kit's install program after you install the Rational product. Installing the activation kit will allow the product to run without expiring. 

Activation if you own Floating licenses 

If you purchased Floating licenses of the products listed above, you have a choice: you can either obtain and install an "activation kit" for each product and install it over the top of your product installation or you can elect to use FLEXlm license keys to manage concurrent usage. (FLEXlm keys are not available for Rational Data Architect and Method Composer).

 * FLEXlm license keys
   
   During the installation of the products listed above, you will be given the option of using FLEXlm license keys to control product usage. FLEXlm license keys are managed through the IBM Rational License Key Center, an on-line license key delivery service that makes it easy for you to generate your Rational license keys. Refer to technote 1250403 [http://www-1.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21250403] for instructions on how to log into the License Key Center if you need help. Versions older than Rational License Server v7.0.1 (for Windows platforms) and Rational License Server v7.0.0.1 (for UNIX or Linux platforms) will not support FLEXlm license keys for these products.

 Attempts to configure the floating license for IBM Rational Integration Tester using IBM Installation Manager leads to the warning 'The server is available, but does not serve license keys for IBM Rational Integration Tester'. 

SYMPTOM
Steps to reproduce:


 1. In Rational Integration Tester client, Click on Start > IBM Installation Manager > Manage Licenses.
    
    
    
 2. Highlight Rational Integration Tester from the List of Installed Products.
    
    
    
 3. Configure floating license support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21403623] for Rational Integration Tester.
    
    
    
 4. Clicking on "Test Connection" results in the below message:
    -------------------
    'The server is available, but does not serve license keys for IBM Rational Integration Tester'.
    -------------------


CAUSE
The PACKAGE ibmrtw block (as shown below) is missing which displays the components of IBM Rational Test Workbench Suite. 
-------------------
PACKAGE ibmrtw ibmratl COMPONENTS="ibmrit ibmrft ibmrpt ibmrpt_pvu"
-------------------


DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
On the license server, launch Rational License Key Administrator. 




 1. Verify if there are 5 lines of 'IBM Rational Test Workbench License' key served by the license server as shown below:
    [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21608473&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21608473&aid=1]
    
    
    
 2. If the lines are not displayed, perform a status enquiry by clicking on Start> IBM Rational> LMTools > Server Status. 
    
    
    
 3. If the line 'Users of ibmrit' is missing, follow the steps below to resolve the problem. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Steps to resolve: 

 1. Navigate to IBM Rational License Key Center [http://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/] website. 
    
    
    
 2. Return and generate the license [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21308308] file for IBM Rational Test Workbench Floating License. 
    
    
    
 3. Download and Import the license file again.
    
    
    
 4. Click on Start > IBM Rational > LMTools > Start/Stop/Reread tab to stop and start the license server.
    
    
    
 5. Next, click on Start > IBM Rational > LMTools > Server Status to perform status enquiry and look for 'Users of ibmrit' line.
    
    
    
 6. Reactivate [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21403623] the floating license for Rational Integration Tester using Rational Installation Manager.

RELATED INFORMATION
#License Requirements for Rational Integration Tester [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21605379]
A simplified Chinese translation is available [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21674212]

AppScan Standard uses the Rational Common Licensing system, and follows it's licensing processes as described below.

Licenses in LKC 
 * 
 * AppScanStandard
 * 

 * Node-locked license
   
   A Node-locked license is tied to the machine where you install the AppScan Standard product. The license allows you to open and use AppScan Standard instances on the particular machine only. You import the license key into the machine using the License Key Administrator, a tool installed by default when installing AppScan Standard (Note: License Key Server is not needed to manage this type of license key). 
   
   In the License Key Center [https://licensing.subscribenet.com/control/ibmr/login] the key is called "IBM Security AppScan Standard Authorized User Single Install License Key ".
   
   If you open the license file (.upd) in a text editor, the license key looks like this:
   
   [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21330869&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21330869&aid=1]
   
 * Floating license
   
   Floating licenses are managed by License Key Server. When having a Floating license you need to install License Key Server, and import it into the License Server using it's tool called License Key Administrator. 
   
   The advantage of this license type is that you can install AppScan Standard on any machines that has TCP/IP connection to the machine where the License Key Server is installed. AppScan pulls a license from the License Server. The license is checked out when you open an AppScan Standard instance, and returned when AppScan Standard is closed. The license usage is described in How AppScan Standard use licenses [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21505444]. 
   
   In the License Key Center [https://licensing.subscribenet.com/control/ibmr/login] the key is called "IBM Security AppScan Standard Floating User Single Install License Key"
   
   If you open the license file (.upd) in a text editor, the license key looks like this:
   [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21330869&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21330869&aid=2]

If you have both licenses installed in your system, AppScan will use the Node-locked license before a Floating license. 

Token license


 * 
 * Token licenses for AppScan products
 * 



How to apply the licenses 
 * 
 * How to import license keys into Appscan Standard
 * 



Common Licensing scenarios 

A) Installing a new AppScan Standard installation 
 *  Obtain your licenses
   The licenses can be obtained from the License Key Center [https://licensing.subscribenet.com/control/ibmr/login]. Check the presentation at: How to generate license keys at License Key Center [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21665366]. 
   Install License Key Server 
   You need to use a License Key Server only if using Floating license keys. If you already have a License Key Server installed to serve another product, you may use that License Key Server for AppScan Standard licensing as well. For a new installation, refer to the technote How to install License Key Server [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21664788]. 
   Import the licenses into License Key Server (Floating) or AppScan Standard (Notelocked). Consult technote How to import license keys into Appscan Standard [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21381093]. 


B) Upgrading AppScan Standard  *  
   AppScan Standard licenses work with all versions of AppScan Standard. Therefore, when you upgrade AppScan Standard to a later version, you do NOT need to upgrade or renew AppScan Standard licenses. 
   
   However, if you upgrade from AppScan Standard version 8.0.0.3 or earlier to version 8.5 or later, there are two possible issues to deal with:  * If using Floating licenses, you will need to upgrade your License Key Server to version 8.1.2 or later. 
    * If your AppScan still uses a legacy Watchfire license, you will need to upgrade them to Rational Common Licenses, since legacy Watchfire licenses do not work with AppScan Standard 8.5 or later. 
   
   
 * 
   

C) Moving AppScan Standard installation to another machine
 *  If using a Nodelocked license, you need to return the current key to the License Key Center [https://licensing.subscribenet.com/control/ibmr/login], and to generate a new license key for the new machine. For details consult the technote: How to transfer License Key Server or license keys [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21686972]. If using Floating licenses and the License Key Server resides on another machine (which is not impacted by the move), you do not need to upgrade either the license keys or the License Key Server. After the installation on the new machine is completed, just point the new License Key Administrator (installed with the new AppScan Standard installation) to the current License Key Server. For details refer to technote: How to import license keys into Appscan Standard [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21381093]. If using Floating licenses, and the License Key Server is installed on the same machine and is going to be moved to the new machine, you will need to return the license keys before generating new keys for the new machine. For details refer to technote: How to transfer License Key Server or license keys [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21686972]. 
   Then proceed with the scenario for A) Installing a new AppScan Standard installation.

response:
Based on the provided context, it seems you are encountering an issue with the licensing for IBM Rational Test Workbench (RTW) 8.5. The key points are:

1. You are getting an error in IBM Installation Manager (IM) stating "The server is available, but does not serve license keys for IBM Rational Integration Tester".

2. You have imported the licenses fine in the Rational License Key Administrator (RLKA) and the Rational Performance Tester (RPT) and Rational Integration Tester (RIT) floating licenses are showing up there.

3. However, the licenses are not showing up in IBM Installation Manager when you try to configure the floating license support for RTW 8.5.

The root cause seems to be that the PACKAGE definition for the IBM Rational Test Workbench Suite components is missing in the license server configuration. This PACKAGE definition is required for the Installation Manager to correctly identify and use the available licenses.

To resolve this issue, you should follow these steps:

1. In the Rational License Key Administrator, verify if there are 5 lines of "IBM Rational Test Workbench License" key served by the license server.

2. If the "Users of ibmrit" line is missing, you need to regenerate the license file for the IBM Rational Test Workbench Floating License from the IBM Rational License Key Center website.

3. Download and import the new license file into the license server.

4. Restart the license server using the LMTools utility (Start/Stop/Reread tab).

5. In IBM Installation Manager, try reactivating the floating license support for Rational Integration Tester.

After performing these steps, the licenses should be properly recognized by the IBM Installation Manager and you should be able to configure the floating license support for RTW 8.5 without any issues.

The v7.0 and later releases of most Eclipse-based IBM Rational products offer two new features designed to help make deployment easier. CAUSE
Effective license usage of Eclipse-based IBM Rational products ANSWER Overview
The v7.0 and later releases of the Rational products listed below use a common activation scheme.
This technote outlines the activation product for the various products to help you get up and running as quickly as possible.
You can now convert a trial (or evaluation) copy of the software to the production version of the same product without having to uninstall and reinstall the product.

Additionally, if you own floating licenses of the products listed below you can now control usage of the products within your enterprise by using FLEXlm-based license keys as an optional feature (not available for Rational Data Architect and Method Composer).
"Activation Kit" or FLEXlm floating license keys required by these Rational products:
** Rational Data Architect support Activation Kits only.
FLEXlm license keys are not offered with these products.
The 7.0 and later versions of the products listed above will expire 30 days after installation.
Rational Application Developer will expire 60 days after installation.
You will need to activate your product in order to use it after the expiration date.
Activation if you own Authorized User licenses
If you purchased an Authorized User license of the products listed above, you simply need to obtain and install an "activation kit" for your product that will convert it to a non-expiring version.
Activation kits are product specific (they are not host-specific like Rational license keys).
This means if you own multiple licenses of one of the products, you only need one activation kit and you can use it on any machine where the product is installed.
For example, if you purchased two copies of IBM Rational Software Architect, you only need to obtain one activation kit and you can install it on both machines running Rational Software Architect.
If you ordered media for your 7.0 or later product, you will find the activation kit on a CD in your software shipment.

If you do not have a CD, you can obtain your activation kit by downloading it from your license account on the IBM Rational License Key Center website [http://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/].
The kit will show up in your license account that offers the v7.0 product license.

Each of the products listed above will have a unique activation kit with the naming convention of "Product Name Multi platform Multilingual Activation Kit", e.g. "IBM Rational Software Architect v7.0 Multi platform Multilingual Activation Kit".
Once you obtain the activation kit, run the activation kit's install program after you install the Rational product.
Installing the activation kit will allow the product to run without expiring.
Activation if you own Floating licenses

If you purchased Floating licenses of the products listed above, you have a choice: you can either obtain and install an "activation kit" for each product and install it over the top of your product installation or you can elect to use FLEXlm license keys to manage concurrent usage.
(FLEXlm keys are not available for Rational Data Architect and Method Composer). Activation kits
If you do not want to use FLEXlm license keys you simply you simply need to obtain and install an "activation kit" for your product that will convert it to a non-expiring version.
Activation kits are product specific (they are not host-specific like Rational license keys).
This means if you own multiple licenses of one of the products, you only need one activation kit and you can use it on any machine where the product is installed.
For example, if you purchased two copies of IBM Rational Software Architect, you only need to obtain one activation kit and you can install it on both machines running Rational Software Architect.
If you ordered media for your 7.0 product, you will find the activation kit on a CD in your software shipment.

If you do not have a CD, you can obtain your activation kit by downloading it from your license account on the IBM Rational License Key Center [http://www-01.ibm.com/software/rational/support/licensing/]website.
The kit will show up in your license account that offers the v7.0 product license.
Each of the products listed above will have a unique activation kit with the naming convention of "Activation Kit for product name", e.g. "Activation Kit for IBM Rational Software Architect".
Once you obtain the activation kit, run the activation kit's install program after you install the Rational product.
Installing the activation kit will allow the product to run without expiring.
During the installation of the products listed above, you will be given the option of using FLEXlm license keys to control product usage.
If you do not choose to use FLEXlm keys, you will need to install an activation kit (see above).
FLEXlm license keys are managed through the IBM Rational License Key Center, an on-line license key delivery service that makes it easy for you to generate your Rational license keys.
Refer to technote 1250403 [http://www-1.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21250403] for instructions on how to log into the License Key Center if you need help.
FLEXlm keys are not available for Rational Data Architect and Method Composer.

If you wish to use floating license keys for v7.0 or later of the products listed above (or for Rational Asset Manager), it is recommended to have a recent version of the Rational License Key Server installed.
Versions older than Rational License Server v7.0.1 (for Windows platforms) and Rational License Server v7.0.0.1 (for UNIX or Linux platforms) will not support FLEXlm license keys for these products.

You can download the most recent versions of the Rational License Key Server and your Rational product(s) from the Passport Advantage Online [https://www-112.ibm.com/software/howtobuy/passportadvantage/paocustomer] account that holds the active maintenance agreement(s) of the Rational product concerned.
IBM products of which the maintenance agreement has expired will no longer be available to download.
For the PA Online software download access requirements see technote http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21396792 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21396792]

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When troubleshooting the execution of an Excel scenario suite with Decision Validation Service (DVS) it can be beneficial to use a minimal sample to help reproduce the issue and ease debugging.
Also in case there is a need to integrate the execution of DVS scenario files with a homegrown or third party test harness, then starting from a minimal sample can ease the integration. 

SYMPTOM
Execution of a DVS scenario suite fails to complete or gives unexpected result.


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The attached sample Rule Studio project consists in a single source file with a main method that performs a DVS run using the tutorial artifacts as an example. The program takes two arguments: first is the ruleset file , second is the excel file. 

The sample can be imported in a Rule Studio workspace with: 

 File > Import > General > Existing Projects into Workspace 

Then choose "Select archive file" and click "Browse" button to point to the dvs-runner.zip file. 

 

The sample can be launched through Rule Studio menu: 

 Run Configurations > Java Application > LocalExcelRunner 

It can also be launched from the command line through ant with ant run (you need to edit build.xml file to set the jrules.home property to point to a local JRules installation directory).

performance; JRules; DVS. Decision Warehouse; DWH; WODM; Decision Validation Services; improvement; Decision Center; Decision Server TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How can I improve the performance of Decision Validation Services (DVS) and Decision Warehouse? 

ANSWER

Improving the performance of DVS testing and the Decision Warehouse involves reducing the size of the execution trace data generated during tests, and also some architectural and environmental configurations that might be suited to your use case. The following are recommendations you can consider incorporating:

Reduce the size of the execution data: 

 * Filter data [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21586717] using the ruleset properties: monitoring.filters and monitoring.inout.filters. 
 * Reduce the BOM serialization overhead:  * Override the toString() method for the ruleset parameters to return minimal information 
    * Set the ruleset property ruleset.bom.enabled to "false" to remove support for BOM based serialization. This property is set to "true" by default when extracting rulesets from Rule Team Server (RTS) and Decision Center, and needs to be explicitly set to "false" in order to deactivate it. (You should set it to "true" if you need to generate an Excel report from a Test Suite/Simulation in RTS.)
   
   Refer to the documentation Optimizing Decision Warehouse for v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global733.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.res%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Execution_Server1571.html]. 
 * Reduce the number of columns in the Excel files by using the Ignore for DVS flag for the arguments in the DVS constructor, in Rule Studio [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global715.html] or Rule Designer [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.rulestudio%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Designer1303.html&resultof=%22Adding%22%20%22ad%22%20%22removing%22%20%22remov%22%20%22columns%22%20%22column%22%20%22from%22%20%22Excel%22%20%22excel%22%20%22file%22%20]. 
 * You can also choose to not write the traces to a database (Decision Warehouse) as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21441394].


Configure Decision Warehouse:  * Manage the production and test environments separately [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html], and use a different Decision Warehouse instance for each environment. 
 * Write asynchronously to Decision Warehouse:  * Using a JMS provider, such as WebSphere MQ or OpenJMS. 
    * Using MDBs or in batch using a ETL tool, such as Clover.ETL or Cognos ETL.
   
   
 * Perform an asynchronous update to Decision Warehouse, as shown in this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global1781.html] for v7.1.x and earlier (and this sample [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.samples%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Samples588.html] for WODM). 
 * Capture the Decision Warehouse trace as an asynchronous operation in application servers supporting thecommonj WorkManager API, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433167]. 
 * Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated. 

Refer to the documentation at Auditing executed decisions [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html] for detailed recommendations for configuring Decision Warehouse. 

Configure Rule Execution Server (RES):  * Do not use a production RES for your tests and simulations. Instead dedicate a separate RES instance for testing. 
 * Set the optimal XU and SSP pool sizes (in v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global206.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]). 
 * Increase the size of the database connection pool for the RES data source. 
 * Dedicate more processing resources to the handling of DVS tests:  * Deploy the SSP along with the RES console on a dedicated server. (By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]). 
    * Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.
   
   
 * Improve RES performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589513].


Configure Rule Team Server (RTS) or Decision Center:  * Install RTS and RES on separate computers. 
 * Reduce the size of the Decision Warehouse trace when running scenario suites from RTS, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438208]. 
 * Improve RTS performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21584855].


Configure Rule Studio or Rule Designer:  * Increase the heap size for DVS testing [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21427125]. 
 * Improve Rule Studio or Rule Designer performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589514].



In addition, refer to the sections Enhancing the performance of Decision Warehouse and Enhancing the performance of Decision Validation Services in the IBM Redpaper: Proven Practices for Enhancing Performance: A Q&A for IBM WebSphere ILOG BRMS 7.1 [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redpapers/pdfs/redp4775.pdf]. RELATED INFORMATION
#Improving the performance of Decision Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]
Improving Decision Validation Services performance [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global206.html]

TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How do you reduce the full execution trace that is stored for Decision Warehouse? 

CAUSE
A lot of information is stored in the field FULL_EXECUTION_TRACE. Over time, when running thousands of executions, the execution trace data will take up too much space in the database. 

ANSWER
Full execution trace can consume a lot of space depending on the size of the ruleset. One recommended way is to apply filters on rulesets to optimize the storage of the execution trace data: 

WebSphere ILOG JRules BRMS V7.1 > Rule Studio > Testing, validating, and auditing rules > Configuring and customizing Decision Warehouse > Optimizing Decision Warehouse [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global733.html] 

Deciding on which **filters to apply is subject to the requirements of each application. If you set the monitoring.filters property, the Decision Warehouse stores only the trace information enabled by the filters that you have set to true. 

In a scenario where you have over 5000 rules within a ruleset and that only 10% of these rules are fired, if you have activated both INFO_TOTAL_RULES_FIRED and INFO_TOTAL_RULES_NOT_FIRED to true, all the rules (fired and not fired) will be logged. You may consider setting INFO_TOTAL_RULES_NOT_FIRED=false to reduce the data on the rules not fired. This greatly reduces the data stored. 

Another possible filter can be INFO_TASKS_NOT_EXECUTED=false. 

*For reducing execution traces logged by DVS, refer to this technote [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438208]instead. 

**Note that in the V7.1 documentation, there is a missing filter INFO_EXECUTION_DATE that provides the execution start date. It is showed in the V7.5 documentation [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSQP76_8.5.0/com.ibm.wodm.dserver.rules.res.managing/topics/tsk_res_config_ruleset_filters.html] and on, but can be used in V7.1 too

RELATED INFORMATION
#Reducing the size of DW trace when running DVS [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438208]
JRules modules and database capacity planning [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461]
Improve Performance of DVS and DW [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21588859]

TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When trying to execute a Decision Validation Services (DVS) test from Rule Designer on a remote installation of Rule Execution Server (RES), a missing files error is seen.



SYMPTOM
When we try to run a DVS test using the Run Configuration from Rule Designer, the Run button remains greyed out. 

The error says: "The RES component of IBM Decision Server, does not seem to be installed. The default classpath might be incorrect and have missing files.." 


CAUSE
 

This error indicates that you have not installed RES on your local machine. Although it is possible to extend a given Eclipse installation with Rule Designer update sites, if the ODM Decision Server product is not installed on the machine the features related to RES and DVS will not be functional.

To conduct DVS tests, even if using remote testing, you need to install ODM Decision Server RES locally, since there is a dependency on RES libraries/variables in Rule Designer. 


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Install ODM Decision Server on the machine where Rule Designer is to be run. 

RELATED INFORMATION
#Testing and simulating rulesets [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v8r5m1/topic/com.ibm.odm.dserver.rules.designer.test/topics/odm_dserver_rules_designer_test.html]
Extend Eclipse with Rule Designer update sites [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSQP76_8.5.1/com.ibm.odm.distrib.config/config_ds_designer/tsk_designer_install.html?lang=en]

* Reduce the BOM serialization overhead:  * Override the toString() method for the ruleset parameters to return minimal information
* Set the ruleset property ruleset.bom.enabled to "false" to remove support for BOM based serialization.
This property is set to "true" by default when extracting rulesets from Rule Team Server (RTS) and Decision Center, and needs to be explicitly set to "false" in order to deactivate it.
(You should set it to "true" if you need to generate an Excel report from a Test Suite/Simulation in RTS.)

Refer to the documentation Optimizing Decision Warehouse for v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global733.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.res%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Rule_Execution_Server1571.html].

* You can also choose to not write the traces to a database (Decision Warehouse) as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21441394].

* Write asynchronously to Decision Warehouse:  * Using a JMS provider, such as WebSphere MQ or OpenJMS.

* Capture the Decision Warehouse trace as an asynchronous operation in application servers supporting thecommonj WorkManager API, as shown in this sample [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21433167].
* Estimate the database capacity [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21430461] that should be allocated.

Refer to the documentation at Auditing executed decisions [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dserver.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DS_Overview83.html] for detailed recommendations for configuring Decision Warehouse.
Configure Rule Execution Server (RES):  * Do not use a production RES for your tests and simulations.
Instead dedicate a separate RES instance for testing.

* Set the optimal XU and SSP pool sizes (in v7.1.x or earlier [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2FDocumentation%2F_pubskel%2FJRules%2Fps_JRules_Global206.html] and WODM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.dcenter.overview%2FContent%2FBusiness_Rules%2F_pubskel%2FInfocenter_Primary%2Fps_DC_Overview2884.html]).
* Increase the size of the database connection pool for the RES data source.
* Dedicate more processing resources to the handling of DVS tests:  * Deploy the SSP along with the RES console on a dedicated server.
(By default tests are run on a single SSP, see Clustering Decision Validation Services [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21425487]).
* Otherwise, distribute the DVS tests [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21502095] on different RES instances.

Configure Rule Studio or Rule Designer:  * Increase the heap size for DVS testing [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21427125].
* Improve Rule Studio or Rule Designer performance [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21589514].

How do you reduce the full execution trace that is stored for Decision Warehouse? CAUSE
A lot of information is stored in the field FULL_EXECUTION_TRACE.
Over time, when running thousands of executions, the execution trace data will take up too much space in the database. ANSWER
Full execution trace can consume a lot of space depending on the size of the ruleset.
One recommended way is to apply filters on rulesets to optimize the storage of the execution trace data:

WebSphere ILOG JRules BRMS V7.1 > Rule Studio > Testing, validating, and auditing rules > Configuring and customizing Decision Warehouse > Optimizing Decision Warehouse [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global733.html]
Deciding on which **filters to apply is subject to the requirements of each application.
If you set the monitoring.filters property, the Decision Warehouse stores only the trace information enabled by the filters that you have set to true.

In a scenario where you have over 5000 rules within a ruleset and that only 10% of these rules are fired, if you have activated both INFO_TOTAL_RULES_FIRED and INFO_TOTAL_RULES_NOT_FIRED to true, all the rules (fired and not fired) will be logged.
You may consider setting INFO_TOTAL_RULES_NOT_FIRED=false to reduce the data on the rules not fired.
This greatly reduces the data stored.
Another possible filter can be INFO_TASKS_NOT_EXECUTED=false.
*For reducing execution traces logged by DVS, refer to this technote [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438208]instead.

TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 While attempting to use last participant support (LPS), the transaction fails with a J2CA0030E logged due to a com.ibm.ws.Transaction.IllegalResourceIn2PCTransactionException. 

SYMPTOM
The following exceptions are logged in the SystemOut.log file:
[8/5/15 10:51:11:469 CDT] 00000036 RegisteredRes E WTRN0062E: An illegal attempt to use multiple resources that have only one-phase capability has occurred within a global transaction.
[8/5/15 10:51:11:938 CDT] 00000036 LocalTransact E J2CA0030E: Method enlist caught com.ibm.ws.Transaction.IllegalResourceIn2PCTransactionException: Illegal attempt to enlist multiple 1PC XAResources
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RegisteredResources.enlistResource(RegisteredResources.java:368)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.TransactionImpl.enlistResource(TransactionImpl.java:2953)
at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.TranManagerSet.enlistOnePhase(TranManagerSet.java:418)
at com.ibm.ejs.j2c.LocalTransactionWrapper.enlist(LocalTransactionWrapper.java:516)
at com.ibm.ejs.j2c.ConnectionManager.lazyEnlist(ConnectionManager.java:1766)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl.lazyEnlist(WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl.java:2061)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.jdbc.WSJdbcConnection.beginTransactionIfNecessary(WSJdbcConnection.java:549)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.jdbc.WSJdbcConnection.prepareStatement(WSJdbcConnection.java:1830)
at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.jdbc.WSJdbcConnection.prepareStatement(WSJdbcConnection.java:1785)


CAUSE
These errors will occur when there are more than one one-phase capable (1PC) resources in an XA transaction. If this is the case, then the WTRN0062E is correct and working as designed.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Review all of your resources (data sources) and verify that you only have one one-phase capable resource in the global transaction. This can be done by referring to the JDBC provider used for each data source. In the WebSphere Application Server Information Center, the article entitled "JDBC provider summary [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSAW57_8.5.5/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/ae/udat_minreq.html]" to determine if any of your data sources are using a non-XA (that is, 1pc) driver. (Note, the link provided is for the WebSphere Application Server v7).


With Last Participant Support (LPS), you are only allowed to have one one-phase capable resource with any number of two-phase capable resources in the same global transaction. Using the administrative console: select Enterprise Applications > your_ear_file >
Last participant support extension, if the box for Accept
heuristic hazard is checked, then the application has LPS enabled.

If you are receiving this message, then the application has more than one 1pc data source involved in the global transaction. The two ways that this may be addressed are
1. change the transaction settings so that one of the 1pc resources is involved in a separate global transaction. See the Information Center article "Setting EJB module ActivitySession deployment attributes [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSEQTP_8.5.5/com.ibm.websphere.base.doc/ass/tasks/tas_depejb2.html]".

2. change from using a non-XA JDBC provider to an XA JDBC provider for one of the data sources that is non-XA. That is, ensure that there is only one 1pc resource in the global tx.

QUESTION
 Why does ADMIN_CMD('load from ...') using JDBC in XA transaction get SQL30090N? 

CAUSE
It is an known current limitation of DB2.

ANSWER
Here is an example message from a jdbctrace.log 

-------------------

[jcc][Thread:WebContainer : 0][SQLWarning@2cab0b03] Stack trace follows
com.ibm.db2.jcc.am.SqlWarning: DB2 SQL Warning: SQLCODE=20397, SQLSTATE=01H52, 
SQLERRMC=SYSPROC.ADMIN_CMD;SQL30090;^@, DRIVER=4.19.49
-------------------

Symptoms:
- It does not throw any exception and the application finished without any problem but 
the data is not actually loaded into the table.
- If the same operation without XA transaction, it is succeeded and loaded data.
- From jdbctrace, SQL20397W and SQL30090N are logged.

The reason why:
The cause of the problem is LOAD does internal commit near the beginning of 
operation. The load internal commit got back SQL30090 error is standard 
behavior in XA environment. So ADMIN_CMD + LOAD does not work on XA.

Workaround:
Unfortunately, there is no way to do ADMIN_CMD + LOAD on XA.

response:
Based on the provided context, there is a known limitation when using the ADMIN_CMD stored procedure with the LOAD operation within an XA transaction environment.

The key points are:

1. When using the ADMIN_CMD stored procedure to execute a LOAD operation within an XA transaction, it can result in the following error:
   - SQL30090N: The LOAD utility cannot be used within a global transaction.

2. This is a known limitation because the LOAD operation performs internal commits, which is incompatible with the XA transaction handling.

3. The provided information states that there is no workaround for this issue. The ADMIN_CMD stored procedure with the LOAD operation cannot be used within an XA transaction environment.

In summary, the main limitation is that the LOAD operation using the ADMIN_CMD stored procedure is not supported within an XA transaction environment due to the internal commit operations performed by the LOAD utility. This is a known limitation and there is no workaround available.
documents_sentences: While attempting to use last participant support (LPS), the transaction fails with a J2CA0030E logged due to a com.ibm.ws.Transaction.IllegalResourceIn2PCTransactionException. SYMPTOM
The following exceptions are logged in the SystemOut.log file:
[8/5/15 10:51:11:469 CDT] 00000036 RegisteredRes E WTRN0062E: An illegal attempt to use multiple resources that have only one-phase capability has occurred within a global transaction.

[8/5/15 10:51:11:938 CDT] 00000036 LocalTransact E J2CA0030E: Method enlist caught com.ibm.ws.Transaction.IllegalResourceIn2PCTransactionException: Illegal attempt to enlist multiple 1PC XAResources at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.RegisteredResources.enlistResource(RegisteredResources.java:368) at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.TransactionImpl.enlistResource(TransactionImpl.java:2953) at com.ibm.ws.Transaction.JTA.TranManagerSet.enlistOnePhase(TranManagerSet.java:418) at com.ibm.ejs.j2c.LocalTransactionWrapper.enlist(LocalTransactionWrapper.java:516) at com.ibm.ejs.j2c.ConnectionManager.lazyEnlist(ConnectionManager.java:1766) at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl.lazyEnlist(WSRdbManagedConnectionImpl.java:2061) at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.jdbc.WSJdbcConnection.beginTransactionIfNecessary(WSJdbcConnection.java:549) at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.jdbc.WSJdbcConnection.prepareStatement(WSJdbcConnection.java:1830) at com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.jdbc.WSJdbcConnection.prepareStatement(WSJdbcConnection.java:1785) CAUSE
These errors will occur when there are more than one one-phase capable (1PC) resources in an XA transaction.
If this is the case, then the WTRN0062E is correct and working as designed.
Review all of your resources (data sources) and verify that you only have one one-phase capable resource in the global transaction.
This can be done by referring to the JDBC provider used for each data source.

In the WebSphere Application Server Information Center, the article entitled "JDBC provider summary [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSAW57_8.5.5/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/ae/udat_minreq.html]" to determine if any of your data sources are using a non-XA (that is, 1pc) driver.
(Note, the link provided is for the WebSphere Application Server v7).
With Last Participant Support (LPS), you are only allowed to have one one-phase capable resource with any number of two-phase capable resources in the same global transaction.
Using the administrative console: select Enterprise Applications > your_ear_file >
Last participant support extension, if the box for Accept
heuristic hazard is checked, then the application has LPS enabled.
If you are receiving this message, then the application has more than one 1pc data source involved in the global transaction.
The two ways that this may be addressed are
1. change the transaction settings so that one of the 1pc resources is involved in a separate global transaction.

See the Information Center article "Setting EJB module ActivitySession deployment attributes [https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSEQTP_8.5.5/com.ibm.websphere.base.doc/ass/tasks/tas_depejb2.html]".
2. change from using a non-XA JDBC provider to an XA JDBC provider for one of the data sources that is non-XA.
That is, ensure that there is only one 1pc resource in the global tx.

question: Why is Connection Refused on the ITCAM Managing Server? ITCAM Data Collector connection to the Managing Server fails with Connection Refused.
documents:
TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The Data Collector (DC) connection may fail with “Connection Refused” if the Managing Server’s(MS) host name can resolve to an IP address that cannot reach the MS. 

CAUSE
The DC obtains the MS kernel’s network address from the MS. If a host name is specified for the kernel, and any of it’s resolved IP addresses cannot reach the MS from the DC, ITCAM’s connection attempt will fail if one of these "invalid” IP’s is used.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Instead of host name, specify a “valid” IP address for the MS in the <MS_HOME>/bin/setenv.sh file, and in ITCAM 6.1, the ms.properties file. This solution usually works except when there is a firewall with Network Address Translation (NAT) enabled. In that case, you must make network changes so that all the resolved IPs can reach the MS. 

Change as directed:

ITCAM 6.0 ( or earlier )
In MS_home/bin/setenv.sh:
KERNEL_HOST01=<ip addr of MS>
KERNEL_HOST02=<ip addr of MS>

ITCAM 6.1
In MS_home/bin/setenv.sh:
KERNEL_HOST01=<ip addr of MS>
am_socket_bindip=<ip addr of MS>
am_socket_exportip=<ip addr of MS>
In MS_HOME/etc/ms.properties, modify “kernel.hosts” specifying MS IP address:
kernel.hosts=<ip addr of MS>CBSPort:RFSPort:RMIPort - usually -
kernel.hosts=<ip addr of MS>9122:9120:9118

Example:
kernel.hosts=9.12.20.220:9122:9120:9118

Example of the error message:
This example is from z/OS, but the problem can occur on any platform.

<PPECONTROLLER, 60014b53-f7e9-db01-4272-2a9f50388c89.511, 
9.12.20.161> Unable to join Kernel WSRT7.pdl.pok.ibm.com:9120 - 
java.net.ConnectException: EDC8128I Connection refused.

response:
Based on the information provided in the TECHNOTE, the main reason for the "Connection Refused" error on the ITCAM Data Collector's connection to the Managing Server is:

The Data Collector (DC) obtains the Managing Server's (MS) network address from the MS. If the hostname specified for the MS kernel resolves to an IP address that cannot be reached by the DC, the connection attempt will fail.

The key points are:

1. The DC gets the network address of the MS kernel from the MS.
2. If the hostname specified for the MS kernel resolves to an IP address that is not reachable by the DC, the connection will fail with "Connection Refused".

The resolution provided is to specify a "valid" IP address for the MS in the setenv.sh file and the ms.properties file, instead of using the hostname. This ensures the DC can reach the MS using a valid IP address.

In cases where there is a firewall with Network Address Translation (NAT) enabled, the resolution is to make network changes so that all the resolved IPs for the MS hostname can be reached by the DC.
documents_sentences: The Data Collector (DC) connection may fail with “Connection Refused” if the Managing Server’s(MS) host name can resolve to an IP address that cannot reach the MS. CAUSE
The DC obtains the MS kernel’s network address from the MS.
If a host name is specified for the kernel, and any of it’s resolved IP addresses cannot reach the MS from the DC, ITCAM’s connection attempt will fail if one of these "invalid” IP’s is used.
Instead of host name, specify a “valid” IP address for the MS in the <MS_HOME>/bin/setenv.sh file, and in ITCAM 6.1, the ms.properties file.
This solution usually works except when there is a firewall with Network Address Translation (NAT) enabled.
In that case, you must make network changes so that all the resolved IPs can reach the MS.
KERNEL_HOST02=<ip addr of MS> ITCAM 6.1 In MS_home/bin/setenv.sh:
In MS_HOME/etc/ms.properties, modify “kernel.hosts” specifying MS IP address:
kernel.hosts=<ip addr of MS>9122:9120:9118 Example: kernel.hosts=9.12.20.220:9122:9120:9118
This example is from z/OS, but the problem can occur on any platform. <PPECONTROLLER, 60014b53-f7e9-db01-4272-2a9f50388c89.511,
To determine IP addresses for a given MS host name [issue on the DC]: nslookup <MS_host_name>
To test basic connectivity, for each IP address listed by NSLOOKUP, issue: ping <ip_address>
